describes: The fifteen stages that produced MESSY STREETS, from 136 billion N-Quads to two LaTeX tables. Most are documented rather than runnable: reproducing them needs 106 GB of reference data and four GPUs. Recording them is the point — the construction method is inspectable even where re-running it is not.

stages.title: Download the Web Data Commons corpus
Parse N-Quads and join address to geo
stages.outputs: Per-class TSV: subject, streetAddress, latitude, longitude
stages.scale: 330,646,780 records with an address; 95,014,529 with coordinates

stages.title: Assemble and apply the filter cascade
stages.note: The stats file IS Table 2. It is shipped at data/pipeline/wdc-filter-stats.json and checked by `messy-streets pipeline show 3`.

stages.title: Load each source into DuckDB, ordered by geohash10
stages.outputs: wdc 6.2 GB, oa 10.7 GB, osd 89.5 GB
stages.note: The geohash ordering is what makes the prefix join tractable. Without this stage there is no existence check.

stages.title: Build the tiers: geohash-6 match plus LLM judges
stages.inputs: wdc, oa, osd databases; Ollama endpoint
stages.outputs: hq_10000, mq_10000, lq_10000 — each with an addresses and a discarded table
stages.needs: 106 GB of reference data, quantised 35B judge on 4 GPUs
stages.note: Three judge roles: street similarity, component validity, and PII — the PII judge runs six times, once per address field.

stages.title: Rejection accounting
stages.inputs: The discarded table of each tier
stages.note: The released tiers ship without their discarded tables, so the rates cannot be recomputed here.

stages.title: Disjointness repair
stages.inputs: hq_10000, mq_10000, lq_10000 and the 1K tiers
stages.outputs: Three tiers of exactly 10,000 mutually disjoint records
stages.scale: 5 replacements for gold, 15 for silver, 2 for raw
stages.note: Existed only as ~30 hand-run DuckDB statements transcribed in a readme. Written as a deterministic script for this artefact — see the directory. `messy-streets sample` shows what its absence cost: nine addresses appear in a benchmark slice but not in the released tier.

stages.title: Divergence scoring and the split threshold
stages.inputs: A tier database plus oa and osd for the reference address
stages.outputs: Jaccard, trigram and Levenshtein similarity distributions
stages.scale: median trigram overlap 0.42, hardcoded into the divergence configs
stages.note: The tier database stores the matched reference street in aux, but the generator re-queries oa/osd by id, so the big databases are still required.

stages.title: Descriptive statistics
stages.note: `messy-streets stats` recomputes these over all 10,000 released records and disagrees with the paper — see ARTIFACT.md.

stages.title: Benchmark slicing
stages.outputs: 10 runs x 100 addresses x 7 precisions per tier
stages.note: Regeneration is not bit-identical: DuckDB's REPEATABLE sampling is version-dependent. `messy-streets sample` checks provenance instead.

stages.title: Geocoder evaluation
stages.note: Raw responses were cached per provider; only the derived geohash predictions are shipped.

stages.title: Table build
stages.outputs: Per-run tables, then mean +/- 2 SEM, then LaTeX

stages.title: Nominatim failure analysis
stages.outputs: A worked table plus twenty screenshots
stages.note: Manual by design: each address was re-queried by hand through the API and the web UI. Evidence, not code.
